conclusion: Normal Triton product evidence is a cross-process proof: ordinary Python plus the external backend establishes driver, fresh compiler/JIT, launcher, loaded runtime, returned tensors, and fallback state, while the fsynced daemon trace establishes GPUDispatcher/ComputeUnit execution and lifecycle. Neither side alone proves the end-to-end result.
decision: Require an ordinary Python entry, fresh Triton compilation, exact package and loaded-DSO provenance, implicitly managed gem5, trace-authoritative simulated execution, client-authoritative returned-tensor oracles, complete cleanup, and zero CPU/NVIDIA fallback. Treat the daemon launcher/compiler/jit/triton fields as daemon-local observations, not as a contradiction of the client-side proof.
invalidated_assumptions: A successful daemon trace alone proves that a normal Triton Python program compiled and launched the kernel.
Daemon-local launcher/compiler/jit/triton false fields disprove client-side Triton execution.
One returned tensor oracle without a simulator trace proves GPUDispatcher or ComputeUnit execution.
Two launches in one Python process necessarily create independent simulator sessions and device resources.
observation: The ordinary Python correctness entry selects gemsim_amd, freshly compiles the pure-b010 5384-byte gfx950 add_kernel, loads the isolated runtime, and implicitly supervises gem5. Two 98432-element launches in one managed session reuse the observed queue, signal, packet VA, and allocation IDs while generations advance. Both returned float32 C=A+B tensors are bit-exact; the daemon records 10476 instruction starts per launch, and fallback remains zero.
question_or_symptom: What evidence proves a normal Triton Python end-to-end launch when the client and daemon observe different parts of the path?
